article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 70% Sativa / 30% Indica
Genetics: Amnesia Haze × OG Kush
Breeder: Dinafem Seeds
THC Content: 15–20%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: Limonene -forward
Primary Flavors: Lemon, citrus, sweet fruit, pine, spice
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid-October
Indoor Yield: 500–600 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 600–800 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Amnesia Kush is what happens when two very different cannabis traditions are deliberately pushed into the same plant. Dinafem paired the soaring cerebral character and commercial productivity of European Amnesia with the resin, strength, earth, and unmistakable presence of American OG Kush. The result does not behave like a simple halfway point between its parents. It grows with the enthusiasm of a sativa, forms unusually substantial flowers for that category, and begins with an energetic cerebral rush before the Kush influence gradually adds physical weight. Its aroma follows the same pattern: bright lemon and sweet citrus appear first, followed by spice, pine, and a deeper earthy note that becomes more apparent once the flower is broken apart.

The cultivar also solves several problems traditionally associated with long-flowering Haze-dominant marijuana . Rather than producing narrow, airy flowers on an uncontrollably lanky plant, Amnesia Kush develops large calyxes, sturdy branches, and substantial yields within a 60–70-day bloom. Dinafem selected it to retain Amnesia’s vitality and mental intensity while introducing enough OG Kush influence to strengthen the structure, shorten internodes, and deepen the finished smoke. For growers who enjoy energetic cannabis but want larger flowers and a more physical finish, this hybrid offers a carefully engineered meeting point between Dutch Haze culture and California Kush breeding.
Genetics and Lineage

Dinafem created Amnesia Kush by crossing Amnesia Haze with OG Kush. The Amnesia side came from genetic material closely associated with the classic Dutch Amnesia line, which the breeder traced through Afghan and Neville’s Haze ancestry. That foundation helps explain the plant’s unusual combination of Haze-like mental effects with thicker flower formation than would normally be expected from a traditional tropical sativa. Amnesia genetics became enormously influential in European cannabis cultivation because they offered strong vigor, high resin production, large yields, and an intense cerebral effect while remaining far more practical indoors than many pure Haze lines.

OG Kush supplies the American side of the pedigree. Although the deeper historical ancestry of OG Kush remains disputed, its breeding influence is unmistakable: dense resin, strong branches, penetrating earthy-pine aromas, fuel-like depth, and a heavy physical component. Dinafem used it not simply to add potency but to reshape how the Amnesia parent behaved in the garden. The resulting plants tend to be sturdier, somewhat more compact, and better able to support large flower clusters than a more conventional Haze-dominant cultivar.

The hybrid remains clearly sativa dominant despite the Kush contribution. Dinafem’s current specification places it at roughly 70% sativa and 30% indica, which matches the way the plant develops and the order in which its effects appear. Vigorous growth, rapid rooting, strong upward momentum, and an energetic opening all point toward Amnesia influence, while the increasingly relaxing finish, denser floral structure, and earthy resin character reveal OG Kush underneath. That division of traits is one reason the strain feels distinct rather than like a generic Haze-Kush cross.
Effects and Experience

The first phase can arrive quickly and with considerable mental energy. Thoughts become more animated, sensory details stand out, and routine activities may feel unusually absorbing. Conversation, music, visual media, writing, or creative work can all fit this portion of the experience because the cerebral effect tends to dominate before the body becomes noticeably heavy. Dinafem specifically characterizes the strain as initially cerebral, and that description captures the way Amnesia influence announces itself almost immediately.

Time changes the experience. The sharp mental lift begins to smooth out, and the Kush side introduces a deeper feeling through the shoulders, back, and limbs. Physical relaxation grows without completely erasing the earlier mental clarity, creating a broad middle stage in which the consumer can feel both stimulated and physically settled. Stronger servings make that transition much more pronounced and can eventually turn the experience from active and social into slower, heavier, and distinctly more introspective.

With breeder-listed THC around 15–20%, Amnesia Kush may appear modest beside some contemporary cultivars, but cannabinoid percentage alone does not describe its intensity. The fast cerebral onset can feel powerful, especially to people sensitive to energetic sativa effects. Excessive consumption may produce dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, racing thoughts, or temporary anxiety before the physical relaxation becomes more noticeable. Moderate dosing better preserves the strain’s defining progression from mental acceleration into body-centered calm.
Medical Benefits

The two-stage effect may appeal to medical cannabis consumers who want mental uplift without committing immediately to sedation. During the earlier portion, the brighter cerebral state may make stress, low mood, or mental fatigue feel less dominant, particularly in low-pressure situations where creativity or social engagement is still desirable. As the session progresses, physical relaxation becomes more important, which may help take attention away from muscular tightness or generalized discomfort.

Larger servings can shift the cultivar toward a much calmer evening experience. The body can feel increasingly heavy, appetite may become more noticeable, and mental activity gradually becomes less urgent. That makes dosage especially relevant: a smaller amount may feel stimulating and functional, while a stronger serving can become far more relaxing. Consumers prone to THC-related anxiety may prefer conservative doses because the early Amnesia-style cerebral rush can become uncomfortable before the Kush side has time to settle it.

Limonene is particularly associated with the strain’s aromatic chemistry and matches its prominent lemon and citrus character. Spicy, piney, herbal, and earthy notes suggest additional terpene complexity, but exact ratios depend on the individual plant and cultivation environment. Medical use is better guided by testing from the actual batch, personal cannabinoid tolerance, medications, and previous response to cannabis rather than assuming every harvest will produce identical effects.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Fresh citrus dominates the opening aroma. Lemon zest is especially noticeable, accompanied by a sweeter fruit quality that gives the flower more depth than a sharp lemon-only strain. The profile can feel bright and almost sparkling when a mature bud is first opened, reflecting the Amnesia parent far more strongly than the earthy Kush side during that initial impression.

Breaking apart the flower reveals the heavier layers. Spice appears beneath the citrus, followed by pine, dried herbs, and earthy resin. OG Kush adds enough depth to prevent the bouquet from becoming purely fruity, while the Amnesia influence keeps the heavier notes from overwhelming the brighter top end. Properly cured flower can therefore shift repeatedly between sweet lemon, spice, evergreen, and soil depending on how it is handled.

The same sequence appears in the flavor. Citrus and sweetness tend to lead on the inhale, while pine, spice, and a darker Kush-like earthiness become stronger through the exhale. Vaporization highlights the lemon and fruit particularly well, whereas combustion gives more weight to spice and resin. Slow drying and patient curing matter because the most volatile citrus compounds can disappear quickly if harvested marijuana is exposed to excessive heat or dried too aggressively.
Growing Information

Amnesia Kush is vigorous enough that indoor growers need to control its size early rather than trying to correct excessive stretch after flowering has begun. Dinafem specifically recommends keeping the vegetative period relatively short when vertical space is limited, with about three weeks of vegetation serving as a practical ceiling in many indoor setups. Plants root quickly, develop energetic vertical growth, and can become surprisingly large if given unrestricted space. Topping, low-stress training , or a screen can help spread that vigor horizontally and keep productive flower sites evenly exposed to light.

Indoor flowering requires approximately 60–70 days, with yields around 500–600 g/m² under optimized conditions. The plant forms large, hard flower clusters built from prominent calyxes rather than the thin, loose buds associated with traditional long-flowering sativas. Dinafem also notes that the cultivar does not require unusually aggressive feeding despite its productivity. Balanced nutrition is preferable because excessive fertilization can compromise aroma and finished flower quality. Strong odor control is worthwhile indoors, as mature plants can become extremely fragrant.

Outdoor cultivation reveals the full scale of the genetics. Plants can approach 3 meters in height and produce roughly 600–800 grams each under favorable conditions, with harvest arriving around mid-October. The sativa-dominant structure handles humidity better than many dense indica plants because it does not retain moisture as readily, making the strain comparatively suitable for humid or tropical environments. Even so, good airflow and protection from prolonged late-season rain remain important once the flowers become large and resinous.
FAQ
What strains make Amnesia Kush?

Dinafem created Amnesia Kush by crossing Amnesia Haze with OG Kush. The Amnesia parent carries strong Dutch Haze influence, while OG Kush contributes American Kush structure, resin, earth, pine, and physical relaxation.
Is Amnesia Kush indica or sativa?

Amnesia Kush is a sativa-dominant hybrid. Dinafem lists it at approximately 70% sativa and 30% indica. Its growth and early cerebral effects strongly reflect the sativa side, while the later physical relaxation shows the OG Kush influence.
How much THC does Amnesia Kush have?
Dinafem lists the cultivar at approximately 15–20% THC with low CBD. Actual cannabinoid levels vary according to phenotype, lighting, cultivation method, harvest timing, and environmental conditions.
What does Amnesia Kush taste like?
The main flavors are lemon, citrus, sweet fruit, spice, pine, and earthy Kush. The brighter Amnesia notes generally appear first, while the darker OG character becomes stronger toward the finish.
How long does Amnesia Kush take to flower?
Indoor flowering takes approximately 60–70 days. Outdoor plants generally reach maturity around mid-October in suitable Northern Hemisphere climates.
Final Thoughts on Amnesia Kush

Amnesia Kush succeeds because neither parent is reduced to a minor background influence. Amnesia Haze controls much of the plant’s vigor, production, citrus aroma, and cerebral intensity, while OG Kush reshapes the structure and adds resin, earth, pine, and an increasingly physical finish. The result feels like a deliberate fusion of two cannabis traditions rather than a strain carrying two famous names for marketing purposes.

Its cultivation traits reinforce that balance. A 60–70-day indoor flowering period is manageable for a predominantly sativa plant, while yields of roughly 500–600 g/m² indoors and 600–800 grams per plant outdoors give the cultivar legitimate production value. Vigorous stretch requires planning, but sturdy branches, substantial flowers, and reasonable nutritional needs keep the plant from becoming unnecessarily difficult.

For consumers, the most memorable quality is the progression of the experience. Bright lemon and sweet fruit introduce a fast cerebral high, spice and pine add depth to the flavor, and the body gradually becomes calmer as the OG Kush influence develops. Amnesia Kush remains a strong example of purposeful hybrid breeding—combining Dutch Haze energy with California Kush weight in a cannabis strain that offers both substantial garden performance and a distinctly layered effect.
